question: In which Indian state do we find caves named after elephant statues found in it?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Elephanta Caves are located on **Elephanta Island** in Maharashtra, near Mumbai.
 
• The name "Elephanta" was given by Portuguese explorers due to a large stone statue of an elephant found on the island.
 
• The caves are a UNESCO **World Heritage Site** and are famous for their rock-cut sculptures dedicated to Lord Shiva.
 
• The most prominent feature of the caves is the **Trimurti sculpture**, depicting a three-faced depiction of Lord Shiva.
 
• The caves date back to the **5th to 8th centuries** and are a significant example of Indian rock-cut art.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India:**

 
 
• India has 40 UNESCO World Heritage Sites as of 2023, including cultural, natural, and mixed sites.
 
• Examples include the Taj Mahal, Ajanta Caves, and Kaziranga National Park.
 
 
 
• **Rock-Cut Architecture:**
 
 
• It refers to structures carved directly into natural rock formations.
 
• Famous examples in India include Ajanta and Ellora Caves (Maharashtra) and Mahabalipuram (Tamil Nadu).
 
 
 
• **Elephanta Island:**
 
 
• Located in Mumbai Harbour, it is also known as **Gharapuri**, meaning "City of Caves."
 
• The island is accessible via ferry from the Gateway of India in Mumbai.
 
 
 
• **Portuguese Influence:**
 
 
• The Portuguese arrived in India in the early 16th century and controlled parts of the western coast, including Mumbai.
 
• They named the island "Elephanta" after the elephant statue they found, which is now preserved in the **Jijamata Udyaan (Mumbai Zoo).**
